Clarity.justification: The paper is well-structured with logical sections (Introduction, Related Work, Method, Results, Discussion). Ideas are clearly articulated, e.g., the three-phase pipeline (Phase A: 3.1%, Phase B: 2.0%, Phase C: 0.1%) and gate thresholds are explicitly defined. Minor issues include hardcoded figure paths in the text and some repetition in the pending experiment description, but overall coherent and easy to follow.

Novelty.justification: Presents a novel systematic measurement of the gap between `>>>` pattern prevalence and subprocess executability in raw Python corpora for LLM training, which prior works (The Stack, phi-1, EffiCoder) did not quantify. The 31× gap finding and import isolation analysis are original contributions, though the core idea of execution filtering builds incrementally on existing heuristic and execution-based approaches.

Soundness.justification: Methods are appropriate and validated: code in scanner.py, results.py, and experiment.log confirms exact results (310/204/10 files across phases, 129.8s runtime, 28/28 tests passing). Error classification and token estimation are consistent. Weakness: H-E1 SFT experiment is designed but not executed, so claims about compile-only benefits remain unverified in this work.

Significance.justification: Addresses an important problem in code LLM data curation (execution-based filtering feasibility at 500M-token scale). The finding that doctest-passing is infeasible (0.004M tokens vs. 500M target) has practical value, but significance is reduced because the SFT quality comparison is pending and the work is a negative result on one filtering strategy without demonstrated model improvements.

strengths: Rigorous three-phase measurement with fully reproducible code and matching experimental logs/results
Clear practical recommendation for compile-only filtering as a scalable alternative
weaknesses: SFT comparison experiment (H-E1) is pending and not executed, limiting empirical claims
Relies on dataset fallback (codeparrot instead of the-stack-dedup) without direct validation on the target corpus
